sound-0.title: Taos Hum
sound-0.summary: A low-frequency hum heard by about 2% of residents; a 1993 congressional-requested study by Los Alamos and Sandia scientists found no source.
evidence: University of New Mexico / national labs investigation (1993).
sound-0.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

sound-1.title: Bristol Hum
sound-1.summary: One of the first widely reported hums; hundreds of residents reported a low droning noise in the 1970s.
sound-1.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

sound-2.title: Windsor Hum
sound-2.summary: A low rumble traced by Canadian government-funded studies to Zug Island industrial facilities in Michigan; it faded after a steel plant idled in 2020.
evidence: Government of Canada and University of Windsor studies.
sound-2.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Probable conventional explanation noted by investigators: Traced to Zug Island steelworks

sound-3.title: Seneca guns
sound-3.summary: Cannon-like booms heard along coasts (Seneca Lake, NY and the Carolinas). Proposed causes include offshore earthquakes, methane release and military aircraft.
sound-3.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

sound-4.title: The Bloop
sound-4.summary: An ultra-low-frequency underwater sound recorded by NOAA hydrophones. NOAA later concluded it was consistent with an icequake.
sound-4.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

rumors.text: The sound came from a gigantic unknown sea creature (popularized by Lovecraft fans).

sound-5.title: Upsweep
sound-5.summary: A seasonal series of upsweeping underwater sounds recorded since 1991; volcanic activity is suspected.
sound-5.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Volcanic origin suspected

sound-6.title: Julia (underwater sound)
sound-6.summary: A loud underwater moan recorded by NOAA; attributed to a large iceberg running aground.
sound-6.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

sound-7.title: Moodus noises
sound-7.summary: Booming sounds known since Native American times; now linked to swarms of tiny shallow earthquakes.
sound-7.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Probable conventional explanation noted by investigators: Microearthquakes

sound-8.title: Barisal guns
sound-8.summary: Gun-like booms heard over the Ganges delta and coast; also called mistpouffers elsewhere. Cause unknown.
sound-8.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

sound-9.title: Kokomo Hum
sound-9.summary: Residents reported a hum and health complaints; a city-funded acoustic study identified industrial fans and compressors as contributors.
sound-9.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Industrial equipment identified

sound-10.title: Auckland Hum
sound-10.summary: A low-frequency hum reported in Auckland, studied by a University of Auckland acoustician.
sound-10.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

sound-11.title: "Sky trumpets" (Kyiv)
sound-11.summary: Viral videos of metallic groaning sounds from the sky; many were shown to be edited with film audio.
sound-11.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Confirmed hoax or fabrication: Many viral clips used dubbed film audio

sound-13.title: Forest Grove / "Mystery boom" swarm (Alabama)
sound-13.summary: Skyquakes: unexplained booms heard over wide areas; some are traced to supersonic aircraft or quarry blasts.
sound-13.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Some traced to jets

sound-14.title: Havana syndrome (first reports)
sound-14.summary: US diplomats reported strange sounds and health symptoms. A 2023 US intelligence assessment judged foreign-adversary involvement "very unlikely"; debate continues.
sound-14.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Explanation proposed but disputed: IC assessment: unlikely adversary weapon

rumors.text: A directed-energy weapon caused the symptoms.

sound-15.title: 52-hertz whale
sound-15.summary: A whale calling at an unusual 52 Hz frequency, tracked by US Navy hydrophones since 1989; species unknown.
sound-15.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Whale; species unknown
